_note: Two separate things are locked here. (1) THE PARITY FIX: y/Y/yes/n/N/no/on/off are booleans in YAML 1.1 and STRINGS in 1.2. R's yaml and PyYAML implement 1.1, so before 0.12.1 `name: n` read as FALSE in R, "n" in Rust, and PyYAML split the difference -- a parameter named `n` could not be bound in R at all. Every binding must now keep these as the source text. (2) A PRE-EXISTING, DOCUMENTED DIFFERENCE: R, Python and Rust are typed parsers and resolve true/false to booleans; the C++ (rapidyaml) and MATLAB parsers keep every scalar as raw text by design, which is what makes timestamps verbatim for free. So `true` is a boolean in the first three and the string "true" in the last two. That is not the bug and is asserted per-binding below. (3) BIG INTEGERS: R's yaml parses a bare integer as a 32-bit R integer, so 835118974644 -- a real `sha1:` in a harbinger_wiki note -- came back as NA while Python and Rust returned the number. R now widens to double when the value does not fit, which serializes unquoted and so matches the other bindings; a verbatim string would have serialized quoted and broken the very parity it was meant to restore. Asserted in the three TYPED bindings only, for the same reason the booleans are: the C++ and MATLAB parsers keep every scalar as raw text by design.
